title: Emerald Horizon Console — route economics & per-route cost walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Emerald Horizon through the Console's per-route usage dashboards, cost decomposition, and recommended optimizations. Discussion focused on mapping their route taxonomy to Redwood routes, using prefix KV caching and batching to reduce token spend, and options for Dedicated capacity vs hosted. Agreed next steps: share pricing scenarios, security docs, and schedule a short bench run for their high-volume search route.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-17 15:00 PST | Duration 46m | Recording available
Attendees: Alex Reed, Priya Malik (Redwood); Jenna Park, Omar Gonzalez, Isaac Chen, Rina Patel (Emerald Horizon)

Summary: quick console tour focused on route-level cost + ops. Deck and security packet were linked in chat.

00:00:06 Alex Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE on the Redwood inference team. Priya is our solutions engineer, she'll lead the console demo.
00:00:12 Jenna Park: Hi, thanks. We've been looking forward to seeing the route economics side — we get a lot of variability across our chat and search routes.
00:00:18 Priya Malik: Great, I'll share my screen. I'm going to start on the per-route dashboard, which is where most customers map their internal endpoints. Quick note: we mapped demo data, not your real data, obviously.
00:00:30 Isaac Chen: Cool, is that the same place where you show model-level token burn?
00:00:34 Priya Malik: Yep, top-left you can pick model or route dimension. So here you can see total tokens, avg latency, error rate, and cost per 1k requests. The route filter is pretty flexible — you can tag routes and do grouping.
00:00:52 Omar Gonzalez: When you say cost per 1k, is that using hosted pricing or does it use a dedicated capacity CP math?
00:01:00 Priya Malik: Good question. By default it's hosted unit economics: compute + model cost. There's a toggle to view Dedicated committed-rate economics — we amortize reserved capacity across baseline throughput and show marginal burst cost.
00:01:18 Rina Patel: Could we see an example with a long-context route? Our summarization route uses 8k tokens on average.
00:01:25 Priya Malik: Sure, filtering to your "summarize" route — you'll notice cost spikes due to sequence length. That's where our recommendations panel suggests quantization and a different batching envelope.
00:01:40 Alex Reed: Also worth pointing out the caching suggestions. For summarize we see limited prefix reuse, but your search route has a lot of prefix overlap so KV caching could remove repeated compute.
00:01:53 Jasper (misc-transcription): KV cash, K V cash — that's a common auto-transcribe error we see.
00:02:00 Jenna Park: Ha, yes we saw that in the doc. How invasive is KV cache to implement on our side?
00:02:06 Priya Malik: Minimal on the app side. You tag the route for prefix caching in the Console, or call the cache API — Redwood handles storing the KV and populating the model's past key values. We'll send the snippet.
00:02:22 Isaac Chen: For the record, our infra is 75% on GCP and we have private VPC peers for data ingress. Anything to know for Private deployment?
00:02:31 Priya Malik: Private has the same Console view via your private control plane. There are VPC peering options and HSM/KMS integrations. We discussed in your security call last month — we'll attach the SOC2 packet.
00:02:45 Omar Gonzalez: Can you show an example of a routing policy? We sometimes want cheap-but-slow and fallback to high-accuracy during spikes.
00:02:52 Priya Malik: Yes — in the routing policies page you can set route priorities, target latency, cost cap. Example: route A uses small quantized model unless latency > 250ms then route to larger model; or fallback to Dedicated pool if hosted saturation > 90%.
00:03:12 Rina Patel: Do we get alerts if a route's quality drifts? We can't have a bad model silently increasing hallucinations.
00:03:18 Alex Reed: Redwood Optimize ties to evals and prompt sets — you can attach a prompt set per route and get regression alerts when key metrics change.
00:03:27 Jenna Park: Nice. Could you also show the cost decomposition by token type? We have multi-turn chat so system+user+assistant split matters.
00:03:34 Priya Malik: Absolutely — switch to token breakdown mode. You can see system prompts and assistant completions trending. For chat-heavy flows assistant tokens dominate and that's where caching helps if prefixes recur.
00:03:50 Isaac Chen: Any concrete numbers: if we enable KV cache on search route, ballpark savings?
00:03:56 Priya Malik: Based on similar customers we typically see 20–50% token reduction for strong prefix reuse. For Emerald's demo we see a simulated 32% token saving on search with a mix of 1.5k average prefix length. We'll include a conservative scenario in the follow-up.
00:04:18 Omar Gonzalez: Ok that helps. What about batching? Does Redwood do automatic continuous batching or do we need to change client behavior?
00:04:25 Priya Malik: The runtime supports continuous micro-batching. From the app you can also set a target throughput and latency SLO. The Console suggests optimal batch sizes per model and shows historical latency impact.
00:04:40 Rina Patel: On the cost side, we're sensitive to token vs latency trade-offs — can we do per-route chargeback for internal teams?
00:04:47 Alex Reed: Yes, per-route chargeback is a standard pattern. You can export route-level cost to CSV or integrate via our billing API to your internal FinOps system.
00:04:58 Jenna Park: Perfect. Can you walk us through a canary rollout? We want to validate quality before rolling to prod.
00:05:04 Priya Malik: In the rollouts tab you configure canary weights, define metrics to guard (latency, error rate, eval score), and set automatic rollback thresholds. We also keep lineage so you can trace which model version served which request.
00:05:22 Isaac Chen: Speaking of model versions — do we have to re-upload models if we do quantized variants?
00:05:27 Priya Malik: You register model variants in the model catalog; quantized versions can be auto-generated by Redwood Optimize or uploaded if you already have artifacts. The runtime will pick the best kernel at runtime.
00:05:39 Omar Gonzalez: Is there an example deck or spreadsheet for dedicated capacity math? We need to justify reserved GPU cost to finance.
00:05:45 Alex Reed: Yes, we have a dedicated capacity worksheet. I'll share the pricing scenarios — one conservative, one aggressive, and an amortized model.
00:05:54 Rina Patel: Could you run a small bench for our high-volume search route? We want to validate latency and cost under realistic QPS.
00:06:00 Alex Reed: Absolutely — proposed pilot: 2-week bench, run search route at 100 QPS, measure 99th latency, tokens saved with KV cache, and unit cost. We can run on hosted or a dedicated trial pool.
00:06:12 Jenna Park: Timeline wise we want to decide by end of January. Is that doable?
00:06:16 Alex Reed: Yes, if we get access and the scope this week we can kick bench next week and report before end of month.
00:06:24 Isaac Chen: A few quick technicals — our requests include an RUID and we use GRPC edge. Any issues?
00:06:30 Priya Malik: We're compatible with GRPC + RUID headers. We'll send the client snippet showing header passthrough.
00:06:38 Omar Gonzalez: Security checklist — SSO and audit logs are musts.
00:06:42 Alex Reed: Understood. We'll attach SOC2 + SAML SSO guide + audit log retention options.
00:06:48 Rina Patel: Are there any competitors in your docs to be aware of that we might benchmark?
00:06:53 Alex Reed: Customers often compare us to Anthropic's hosted endpoints, Vertex AI for managed infra, and a few self-hosted runtime vendors. We'll include a short competitive comparison, but we generally focus on production ergonomics and cost controls.
00:07:08 Jenna Park: That makes sense. Anything else on the console before we wrap?
00:07:13 Priya Malik: I'll show the 'Recommendations' card — it lists batching + quantization + route split suggestions and an expected cost delta. Note these are heuristics based on your traffic shape.
00:07:27 Alex Reed: Okay, quick recap and next steps.
00:07:31 Alex Reed: Action items: I'll send pricing and dedicated worksheet; Priya will share snippets for KV cache and gRPC headers; we'll propose pilot dates.
00:07:42 Jenna Park: Thanks everyone. Look forward to the bench numbers.
00:07:46 Alex Reed: Thanks, bye.

End of recording.
